title: Mini-cluster flood runner and adaptive kernel spectator
author: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Adds a deterministic mini-cluster flood runner (mini-flood) for reproducing multi-tenant micro-interference and saturation patterns on small local clusters, plus an adaptive kernel spectator that collects per-kernel execution occupancy and produces a prioritized kernel heatmap used by the model-registry and serving-runtime teams.

Motivation: Several tail regressions in the past quarter appeared only under multi-tenant interference on small clusters (on-prem and CI), which we could not reproduce reliably with existing workload runners. This PR implements a lightweight, deterministic flood driver that: (1) can bootstrap multiple simulated tenants with independent token distribution profiles, (2) supports warmup vs steady-state phases, and (3) injects synchronized micro-bursts to surface scheduling and kernel contention issues. The companion spectator records per-request per-kernel timings and occupancy counters and emits an aggregated kernel-priority report compatible with the benchmark-lab reporting pipeline.

Description/changes:
- New runner: bench/runners/mini_flood/mini_flood.py
  - Orchestrates N synthetic clients across M worker nodes (configurable).
  - Supports profile types: short-chat, long-completion, sparse-embed.
  - Deterministic RNG seed to reproduce traces across runs.
  - Phase scheduler with configurable phase lengths and burst intensity.
- New spectator: bench/telemetry/kernel_spectator/collector.go
  - Pulls per-request kernel samples from an in-process shim (runtime shim hooks added here), aggregates occupancy, tail-latency contributions, and kernel hit ratios.
  - Produces a kernel-priority JSON that includes suggested compilation and routing hints (hot, warm, cold).
- Runtime shim hooks (small API surface) added so the spectator can subscribe to kernel events: runtime/observability/kernel_events.h and runtime/observability/kernel_events_stub.cc
- Reporting connector: bench/reporting/connectors/kernel_report_uploader.py
  - Uploads kernel-priority artifacts to the benchmark-lab reporting pipeline (S3 + metadata). Supports dry-run mode.
- CI/workflow: .github/workflows/mini_flood_ci.yml
  - Lightweight matrix that runs the runner in a dockerized mini-cluster and validates reproducibility checks.

Commit summary:
- 1st commit: high-level runner scaffold and deterministic scheduler
- 2nd commit: kernel spectator prototype and event API
- 3rd commit: reporting connector and uploader
- 4th commit: CI workflow and test fixtures
- 5th commit: docs and usage examples

Files changed (high level):
- bench/runners/mini_flood/mini_flood.py: main runner + CLI
- bench/runners/mini_flood/profiles.yaml: sample token-distribution profiles
- bench/telemetry/kernel_spectator/collector.go: core aggregator
- runtime/observability/kernel_events.h: shim header for kernel event hooks
- runtime/observability/kernel_events_stub.cc: default no-op implementation for non-instrumented builds
- bench/reporting/connectors/kernel_report_uploader.py: uploader
- .github/workflows/mini_flood_ci.yml: CI workflow

How to run locally (short):
1) docker-compose up -d mini-cluster (see examples/docker-compose-mini.yml in the branch)
2) pip install -r bench/runners/mini_flood/requirements.txt
3) python bench/runners/mini_flood/mini_flood.py --nodes 3 --clients 12 --profile short-chat --phase-length 60 --seed 42 --output ./artifacts/run-42
4) python bench/reporting/connectors/kernel_report_uploader.py --input ./artifacts/run-42/kernel-priority.json --dry-run

Notes on determinism and CI: The runner uses a seeded PRNG and fixed request timing offsets to make runs reproducible across machines. Network jitter and host scheduling are still sources of variability; CI workflow runs the same seed twice and asserts that kernel-priority top-3 entries are stable. Benchmarks: Added a small stability test demonstrating reproducible top-k kernel lists on a 3-node mini-cluster. Observed delta across two runs (same seed) on CI: top-5 overlap = 100%, kernel-priority checksum stable. Backwards compatibility: The runtime shim provides a no-op default implementation so builds that don't wire the spectator continue to work. The collector forwards empty artifacts when no kernel events are present.

Checklist:
- [x] Runner core implemented
- [x] Spectator implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Reporting connector
- [x] CI workflow
- [x] Documentation and example runlog
- [x] Basic reproducibility assertion in CI
commits: 5 commits: 1) scaffold mini_flood runner and CLI; 2) initial kernel_spectator collector and event API; 3) uploader and reporting connector; 4) CI workflow and reproducibility test; 5) docs and examples (squash-ready)
review_conversation:
Diego Martinez (reviewer): Can the spectator handle merged kernel invocations (batched kernels) or only per-invocation samples?
Aisha (author): It aggregates per-invocation samples but tags batched kernels with batch_size metadata; we report both aggregate occupancy and per-batch histograms.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): CI flaked once on the reproducibility assertion (run 1 vs run 2 mismatch). What changed?
Aisha: Flake was caused by a race in the test fixture startup; added a deterministic startup barrier and bumped the wait timeout. Verified two consecutive runs now pass in the matrix.
Priya Shah (reviewer): Looks good but please add a short README with safety guidance for running the flood runner in shared CI/CD.
Aisha: Added README and an explicit --dry-run flag on the uploader; updated PR.
Diego: Approve after small nits fixed.
Liam: Approve.
PR merged by Samira Patel via squash with message: "mini-flood runner + kernel spectator: reproducible mini-cluster interference runner and kernel priority reporter"
release_notes: Adds a deterministic mini-cluster flood runner and an adaptive kernel spectator that outputs kernel-priority artifacts for targeted kernel tuning. Useful for reproducing multi-tenant interference and guiding kernel optimization.
